A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-attention Hessian study, with readable equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably; v1's experimental Appendix E becomes Appendix F in v2, alongside new appendices.

before.justification: Figures 1, 3, and 4 report original Hessian visualizations and scaling experiments on five-digit addition, with experimental details in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports revised Hessian scaling experiments and additional depth-dependent Transformer, linear-attention, and MLP results in Figures 6–8 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The work retains its self-attention formulation and Hessian decomposition approach without introducing a new learning or inference procedure. Appendix E extends the theoretical analysis to standard multi-head attention and factorized value matrices; these are analytical extensions rather than a newly proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use five-digit addition framed as next-token prediction, with sequence length 17. The added depth, linear-attention, and MLP experiments retain this task; they change model configurations and analyses rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds linear MLPs as an empirical comparison for linear self-attention in Figures 7–8. v1's MLP comparison was theoretical. The existing empirical comparison between classical and linear self-attention is retained.

E3.justification: Figure 3's stated setup changes from the first layer of a 10-block Transformer using 40 samples to a single-block Transformer using 64 sequences. New protocols examine Transformers at depths 2–5, linear attention at depths 1–3, and MLPs at depths 1–4; the latter two use MSE rather than the main experiments' cross-entropy loss.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds layer-resolved depth analyses testing whether single-layer predictions generalize inside deeper Transformers, whether linear-attention Hessians exhibit the predicted depth dependence, and whether MLP scaling remains depth-independent. These substantially extend v1's normalization and softmax-removal analyses. Figure 5 only redisplays Figure 3a's data.

E5.justification: For the scaling experiments, v1 reports 10 repetitions with means and standard deviations; v2 reports 20 repetitions with means and standard errors of the mean. This is an explicit change in reported repetition count and uncertainty reporting, beyond changes in plotted values.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces measurements under revised settings: for example, the fitted Pre-LN value outer-product exponent changes from -0.6 to -1.2, and the query functional exponent from -1.1 to -0.7. Figures 6–8 add substantial results on internal-layer behavior, linear-attention depth scaling, and quadratic MLP scaling. These are revised-setting and newly reported results.

T1.justification: New Appendix E derives multi-head Jacobians, establishes zero inter-head functional-Hessian blocks, and analyzes factorized value parameters. Lemma D.2 adds an explicit full-rank assumption for query and key matrices. v2 also corrects the vectorization identity in Equation (13) and the final Z2 expression in Appendix C, while retaining the main single-layer theorems.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: exact single-layer self-attention Hessian expressions, heterogeneous data/weight/attention-moment dependencies, and the structural influence of softmax and query-key parameterization. The additional analysis supports this existing contribution framework.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the description of MLP input dependence from linear to quadratic in Section 2. Appendix G adds applicability qualifications: higher-order depth effects emerge beyond the practical input-scale range, internal-layer value functional blocks need not vanish, and numerical instability limits the linear-attention experiments. The central interpretation of Hessian heterogeneity remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility statement and a code-access link absent from v1. Appendix F more explicitly documents Pre-LN placement, regression on logarithmic coordinates, and implementation settings for the added controls. Dataset construction, initialization, principal dimensions, and the Hessian-norm estimator were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds connections to gradient imbalance through Liu et al. (2020), tensor-network reasoning through Bridgeman and Chubb (2017), and additional mathematical and softmax references. It replaces the CurvLinOps-related citation and removes Dauphin et al. (2024). The central positioning as an exact theoretical Transformer-Hessian analysis remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits prose, standardizes terminology and references, expands explanations of commutation matrices and Jacobians, and adds an appendix contents list and reproducibility statement. Experimental setup moves from Appendix E to F. The main section sequence and most retained exposition and proof structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the graphical presentation with multi-panel depth comparisons in Figures 6–8. Figure 3 is redrawn with revised axes, trend guides, and a practical-range marker, omitting the zero functional-value panel. Figure 4 gains explicit comparison labels, while Figure 5 presents Figure 3a's data on linear axes. Table 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the connection between theory and empirical validation. v1 used a 10-block model for Figure 3 while describing the value functional block as zero; v2 aligns the main check with a single block and separately documents nonzero internal-layer blocks and other depth-dependent departures. The new depth and MLP controls establish meaningful applicability boundaries. Multi-head analysis, explicit rank assumptions, corrected formulas, and code-access information further improve rigor and reproducibility.
